cards.explanation: The answer is Joseph, friends. The Lord GOD says, "Joseph shall receive two portions." (Ezekiel 47:13) Joseph's two sons were Manasseh and Ephraim (Genesis 41:51-52), and when the tribes get listed later, each of those two has a strip of his own (Ezekiel 48:4-5).

The answer is True! God says it plainly: "You are to divide it equally among them." (Ezekiel 47:14) No tribe gets a bigger slice than the rest. That's the kind of fairness that keeps everybody happy at a cookie table too.

The answer is that He swore to give it to their forefathers. God says, "Because I swore with an uplifted hand to give it to your forefathers, this land will fall to you as an inheritance." (Ezekiel 47:14) The reason is a promise God made. I love that, friends, because a promise from Him is the best deed you could ever hold.

The answer is foreigners who live among them and have children, friends. God says, "You shall allot it as an inheritance for yourselves and for the foreigners who dwell among you and who have children." (Ezekiel 47:22) So the guest list got longer. It includes the foreigners living among them, and I just love that.

The word is native-born, friends! God says, "You are to treat them as native-born Israelites; along with you, they shall be allotted an inheritance among the tribes of Israel." (Ezekiel 47:22) Same treatment, same inheritance. No second-class anything.

The answer is False. God says, "In whatever tribe a foreigner dwells, you are to assign his inheritance there…" (Ezekiel 47:23) There's no special foreigner section. He gets his land right in the tribe he lives in, alongside his neighbors.

The answer is the sanctuary, friends! God says of the set-apart portion, "In the center will be the sanctuary." (Ezekiel 48:8) Verse 10 says it again: "In the center will be the sanctuary of the LORD." So it sits right in the middle of the portion set apart.

The answer is the descendants of Zadok. God says it is for "…the descendants of Zadok, who kept My charge…" (Ezekiel 48:11) Those are the consecrated priests. God adds that they "…did not go astray as the Levites did when the Israelites went astray."

The answer is True. God says Zadok's descendants "…did not go astray as the Levites did when the Israelites went astray." (Ezekiel 48:11) That's a heavy line, friends, and I think it's a sober one. The text puts it right beside the ones who kept His charge.

The first blank is sell, friends! God says, "They must not sell or exchange any of it, and they must not transfer this best part of the land…" (Ezekiel 48:14) That means no selling, no swapping and no handing it over. The second blank is holy! The verse ends, "…for it is holy to the LORD." (Ezekiel 48:14) That's the reason given. This is the best part of the land, and it belongs to Him.

The answer is False. The text says, "The workers of the city who cultivate it will come from all the tribes of Israel." (Ezekiel 48:19) Not one tribe, but all of them. That's a lot of different hands on the city's land.

The answer is the prince, friends! God says, "The remaining area on both sides of the holy portion and of the property of the city will belong to the prince." (Ezekiel 48:21) His land runs out east and west toward the borders. And the holy portion and sanctuary stay in the middle of it all.

The answer is the tribes of Israel! God says, "…the gates of the city will be named after the tribes of Israel." (Ezekiel 48:31) Twelve gates, three on each side, and every one carries a tribe's name. The north side has "the gate of Reuben, the gate of Judah, and the gate of Levi." That's a whole city with the family name on the door.

The answer is False. The east side has "the gate of Joseph, the gate of Benjamin, and the gate of Dan." (Ezekiel 48:32) Manasseh and Ephraim, Joseph's sons (Genesis 41:51-52), each get a portion in the land (Ezekiel 48:4-5), but the gate carries their father's name, Joseph.

The answer is THE LORD IS THERE, friends! That's the last line of the whole vision: "…from that day on the name of the city will be: THE LORD IS THERE." (Ezekiel 48:35) After all those measurements, gates and borders, that's the name the city gets. I think that's a pretty fine way to end.
